findings.message:
Relative link destinations are sanitized as prose

Only absolute HTTP(S)/FTP and `www.` starts are shielded. A valid relative link such as `[link](/foo:fixes:#123)` reaches the keyword regex, which removes `fixes:` and changes the URL.

src/github/text.ts:11-15

Parenthesis heuristic corrupts angle-delimited URLs

`findUrlEnd` stops at any `)` with zero nesting, even inside an angle-delimited Markdown URL. For `[link](<https://example.test/foo)Fixes:#123>)`, it treats URL content as the link close and sanitizes `Fixes:`.

src/github/text.ts:29-31

summary: URL shielding still rewrites valid Markdown URL destinations.
